issues.detail: The Hebrew phrase 'אוֹ אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר תֵּצֵא מִמֶּנּוּ שִׁכְבַת זָרַע' means 'or a man from whom an emission of semen goes out' (i.e., a man with a seminal emission, a bodily discharge, not '行淫' which means 'sexual immorality/fornication'). The Chinese '行淫' adds a moral/sexual-sin connotation not present in the Hebrew, which is a neutral ritual impurity term. This changes the meaning for a Chinese reader.

The Hebrew 'וְהַנֹּגֵעַ בְּכָל טְמֵא נֶפֶשׁ' is rendered as '凡觸摸一切不潔性命的' which is acceptable, but the final clause 'לֹא יֹאכַל' (shall not eat) is implied in the Chinese '都不可吃聖所的物' — this is fine. However, the phrase 'אוֹ אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר תֵּצֵא מִמֶּנּוּ שִׁכְבַת זָרַע' is rendered as '或是那有人行淫後裔從他而出的人' — '後裔' (offspring/descendant) is an addition; the Hebrew says 'emission of semen' (שִׁכְבַת זָרַע), not 'offspring'. This adds a concept not in the Hebrew and changes the meaning.
